publish-boundary-test.ref: server/killSwitchSharing.test.ts (13) + server/publishChokePoint.test.ts (13). socialPublish.ts changed in two ways and both are covered. (1) The kill-switch check was EXTRACTED to killSwitchBlockedPlatforms so igAutopost — an autonomous cron measured at 116 live posts in prod — could share the operator's emergency stop instead of bypassing it. killSwitchSharing.test.ts pins the guard's decisions (global / publishing / per-platform, the DENY audit record naming WHICH switch fired, and the deliberate fail-open when switch state is unreadable) AND pins that the extraction left publishToSocial behaviourally identical — including the partial-block case where one platform is stopped and the other still publishes, which is the behaviour most likely to be lost in an extraction. (2) A `link` field was added, because its absence was WHY nickActions.socialPost reached around the door to metaSocial.socialPost; pinned through to postToFacebook. publishChokePoint.test.ts holds the claim gates at contentAdmin.publishCarousel and nickActions.socialPost, and adds a structural sweep asserting no NEW file can import the low-level publishers — the part that makes it stick, since adStudio was fixed alone on 2026-07-25 and this identical defect survived on three other surfaces. Both structural assertions red-green verified: planting a file that imports postToInstagram fails the sweep by name; removing igAutopost's guard branch while keeping the call fails its pin. CADENCE IS NOT CLAIMED — this change deliberately did NOT apply the feed cap to igAutopost, because policy v7 sets maxFeedPostsPerDay=2 while the autoposter has been doing 3/day on 8 of the last 14 active days, and that conflict is the operator's to resolve, not this PR's to decide silently. PR #1127.

cron-fail-closed.ref: server/__tests__/cron-cadence.test.ts (26), mutation-verified. The cron path changed here is a CADENCE gate, and the new non-operator decision point is claimOncePerShopDay() in server/cron/scheduler.ts — it decides whether a business-hours job may run today. It FAILS CLOSED at every exit: outside business hours -> false; getDb() null -> false; any thrown error -> a log.warn carrying errorId CRON_DAILY_CLAIM_FAILED, then false. That direction is deliberate and asymmetric: two of the four jobs on this path (referral-loop-closer, vip-auto-recognition) send customer SMS, so a DB blip returning `true` would re-fire them on every pass of the 2h tier. A duplicate text costs more than a missed day. The claim also sits INSIDE acquireCronLock(job.name) and releases the lock when it declines — two pods that each read 'not yet run today' would otherwise both claim and both send, which is the v1.7 duplicate-SMS regression this repo already paid for. Tests pin all three properties directly: fail-closed on unreadable claim (asserts the `if (!d) return false` exit and a catch that returns false), the claim-after-lock ordering, and the lock release on a declined claim. Three mutations were verified to turn the suite RED and the file restored byte-identical after each: a businessHoursOnly job moved back into the 24h daily tier (1 fail), the claim moved before the lock (2 fails), and the ET clock replaced by a hardcoded -05:00 offset (5 fails). Full serial suite green: 376 files passed / 2 skipped, 4,622 passed / 50 skipped / 1 todo, exit 0.

operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES, on a phone. (1) A bad admin deep link now says so. Opening /admin?tab=<anything-unknown> shows an amber "That link went nowhere" strip naming the slug, above the section, dismissible, and cleared automatically by the next deliberate navigation. Previously the identical URL landed on Today in silence, indistinguishable from opening Today on purpose — so a renamed section or a stale saved link looked like normal behaviour. Reproducible with no production read: open /admin?tab=zzz. The legitimate cases are unchanged and covered by client/src/__tests__/adminUnknownSlug.test.ts (9): a bare /admin, a section id, an alias, the legacy ?section= parameter, and a compound redirect all resolve silently. (2) A new round button appears bottom-right on phones only, opening the existing command palette straight into a browsable list of all 32 quick actions. Before this the palette opened to an empty sheet you had to type into, and its only trigger sat in the top bar outside the thumb arc — so on the operator device the actions were reachable only by guessing a search term. Desktop is unchanged: the button is lg:hidden and Cmd+K still works. ActivityPulse now stacks 5.75rem higher on mobile so its pills cannot cover or swallow taps on that button during an SSE burst. (3) Sidebar and shell switched to h-dvh/min-h-dvh; the visible change is that the sidebar footer ("Back to site") is no longer cut off under browser chrome in Safari-as-a-tab, the minimal-ui fallback, and installed Android PWAs. NOT claimed for true iOS standalone, where 100vh already equals 100dvh. (4) The mobile sidebar scrim lost its backdrop blur; it is still bg-black/60. Full pnpm run verify exit 0; 33 tests across the three admin registry specs.

capability-ledger-updated.deferred: No capability gains or loses a state, so no ledger entry is edited. The rule fires on three files under server/services/**. (1) veoStudio.ts: one thrown-error STRING, "cannot authenticate" -> "authentication failed", so shared/providerErrors.ts classifies a missing Veo credential as AUTH_INVALID (PAUSE_PROVIDER, terminal on attempt 1) instead of UNKNOWN (RETRY_BACKOFF, consumesAttempt) and stops burning three attempts on a fault no retry can fix. (2) generationLedger.ts: adds a veo_second_720p rate and a reelClipCostUsd(provider) helper. (3) reelPipeline.ts: the two reel spend sites now price by the provider that actually rendered, instead of a flat seedance constant. All three are ACCOUNTING and FAILURE-CLASSIFICATION corrections — no new surface is exposed, no capability changes operationalState, and the healthy generation path is behaviourally identical. Evidence for the spend half is under render-spend-trajectory. VERIFIED AGAINST PROD THIS SESSION and NOT fixed in code, because it is an env change on a live publishing pipeline and therefore the operator's call: Railway MAINnicks-tire-auto has REEL_VIDEO_PROVIDER=higgsfield while REEL_GENERATION_ENABLED, REEL_AUTOPOST_ENABLED and REEL_PUBLISH_ENABLED are all true — and the Higgsfield session is expired. reelPipeline.ts:81-82 returns an explicit pin UNCONDITIONALLY, bypassing every credential check, so generation is pointed at a dead provider. Veo is ready: probe-veo-generate.ts run under railway run (free metadata-only mode) returned probeVeoConnection OK for veo-3.1-fast-generate-preview with S3_BUCKET set. Note this contradicts scripts/watch-veo-cutover.mjs, which states REEL_VIDEO_PROVIDER was deleted from Railway on 2026-07-31 — it is present today, so the cutover was reverted or re-added.

render-spend-trajectory.ref: server/reelClipCost.test.ts (12) — trajectory through the service boundary, not just the arithmetic. The defect was never in a formula: COST_ESTIMATES_USD had no veo key and BOTH reel spend sites multiplied by seedance_clip regardless of provider, so a pure-function test would have passed against the broken code. The trajectory block therefore drives cost -> reserve() -> policy check -> PERSISTED row through a mocked ledger db and asserts the persisted estimatedCostUsd. Three cases carry it: a veo reservation persists beats x 8s x $0.10 AND is asserted NOT equal to the seedance price (the exact number the old code booked); a higgsfield reservation still persists the seedance price, so the fix did not simply reprice everything; and — the one that makes it a money bug rather than a reporting one — a daily ceiling set deliberately BETWEEN the two prices rejects the veo reservation with BUDGET_DAILY_EXCEEDED while the identical job priced as higgsfield passes. That gap is exactly how much budget guard the undercount was giving away. The fake ledger computes its re-sum aggregate FROM the persisted rows rather than a hard-coded total, so the budget branch is driven by the reserved amount; with a constant the test could not distinguish the two prices at all. Malformed-override cases (empty string, non-numeric, on both REEL_VEO_USD_PER_SECOND and REEL_VEO_DURATION) assert cost > 0, because Number("") is 0 and a zero would report every reel as free and disable the ceiling entirely — a worse failure than mispricing. Env is passed explicitly to every case rather than mutating process.env, per the singleFork serial-suite hygiene rule. selectiveRepair deliberately NOT changed: it imports generateReelClipVideo from ./higgsfieldStudio directly, so its hardcoded provider:"higgsfield" is correct. NOT CLAIMED: the veo per-second rate is a published Google figure multiplied by an ASSUMED 8s default duration, not a reading of what was actually billed; rows stay flagged isEstimate and both inputs are env-tunable.
